title: SayDo: Benchmarking the Safety of Frontier Models from Chat to Closed-Loop Robot Control
abstract: arXiv:2611.30957v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Frontier vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used as high-level robot controllers, yet their safety is evaluated almost entirely in text. We introduce SayDo, a benchmark that assesses the propensity of frontier models to cause harm in embodied contexts. SayDo comprises eleven laboratory and household tasks that pair a benign instruction with a hazard latent in the scene. Tasks are implemented in six settings along an embodiment gradient, from chat questions about an imagined robot to closed-loop control of a simulated robot arm. Benign controls, safe-alternative variants and scripted operator pushback complement each task. Across six open- and closed-weight VLMs and 11,480 episodes, hazardous-action rates rise from 14% in chat to 47% in the simulator, and from 2% to 80% for the most affected model. The increase is largely driven by open-weight models. We find that models flag hazards before acting in 73% of unsafe episodes a

translated_title: SayDo：从聊天到闭环机器人控制的前沿模型安全性基准测试
translated_abstract: 前沿视觉语言模型（VLM）正越来越多地被用作高层机器人控制器，但其安全性评估几乎完全局限于文本环境。我们提出了SayDo，这是一个评估前沿模型在具身场景中造成危害倾向的基准。SayDo包含十一个实验室和家庭任务，每个任务将一条良性指令与场景中潜藏的危险配对。任务沿着具身梯度在六种设置中实现，从关于想象机器人的聊天问答到模拟机械臂的闭环控制。每个任务还配有良性对照组、安全替代变体以及脚本化的操作员劝阻。在六种开源和闭源权重的VLM上进行的11,480个回合测试中，危险动作率从聊天场景的14%上升到模拟器中的47%，而受影响最严重的模型则从2%飙升至80%。这一增长主要由开源权重模型驱动。我们发现模型在73%的不安全回合中在行动之前就已识别出危险……
tldr: 提出了SayDo基准，通过从聊天问答到闭环机器人控制的具身梯度设置评估前沿VLM的安全性，发现危险动作率随具身程度加深从14%显著升至47%，揭示了文本安全评估与真实具身风险之间的巨大差距。
en_tdlr: We introduce SayDo, a benchmark evaluating frontier VLM safety across an embodiment gradient from chat to closed-loop robot control, showing hazardous-action rates rise from 14% in chat to 47% in simulation.
